newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open flat, eye on week's data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open flat, eye on week's data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in very quiet trade on Monday, with the market seen trading flat ahead of a series of economic reports which will be released beginning tomorrow, analysts said.

"There's not much happening. Obviously there's a lot of big numbers this week in the U.S.," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services. "I would guess it would trade very quietly today."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$120.13 to yield 6.468 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.45 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to two basis points from one at Friday's close.
Key economic releases out this week include the U.S. employment cost index out tomorrow, real Canadian and U.S. gross domestic product data out Thursday and U.S. non-farm payrolls data out on Friday.

Ahead of the releases the Canadian market is seeing some curve flattening trade. Allan said the shift is being caused by speculation that weakness in the dollar will prompt the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates.
The central bank last hiked rates on June 26, partly to offset a weaker dollar.

"I don't think it (the bond market) will trade actively today at all. We'll see what the employment cost index numbers come in tomorrow. That's one of (Fed Chairman Alan) Greenspan's favorite ones," said Allan.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.04 to C$109.60 to yield 5.928 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.16 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was 23 basis points, unchanged from Friday.
